He is withdrawn, exhausted and frightened, and it takes Suze very little time to work out why: he sees the dead exactly as she does, has no idea what that makes him, and has been told by the adults around him that something is wrong with him.
characters.name: Jack Slater

characters.description: Jack's older brother, a poised, wealthy teenager staying at the resort for the summer. He is charming, attentive and interested in Suze from the moment he meets her, and he behaves throughout as though he already knows more about her than he should.
characters.name: Paul Slater

characters.description: The ghost of a young woman from a prominent nineteenth-century Californian family, still dressed for the century she died in, elegant and used to being obeyed. She was engaged to her own cousin, Hector de Silva, who disappeared in 1850 before the wedding. She appears to Suze with one demand: that the digging in the Ackermans' backyard stop.
characters.name: Maria de Silva

characters.description: The ghost of the man Maria married after her cousin vanished, physically imposing and with an ugly reputation in his own lifetime. He is dangerous in a way Maria is not: she gives the orders and he carries them out.
characters.name: Felix Diego

characters.description: Suze's stepfather, whose summer project is a hot tub in the backyard, which means excavating ground that has not been disturbed since the house was built.
characters.name: Andy Ackerman

characters.description: A television journalist, remarried and settled in Carmel, who is pleased her daughter has found summer work and has no idea what else her daughter does.
characters.name: Suze's mother

characters.description: The eldest stepbrother, working a summer job and otherwise asleep. Suze calls him Sleepy.
characters.name: Jake Ackerman

characters.description: The stepbrother in Suze's own year, a wrestler and a reliable irritant. Suze calls him Dopey.
characters.name: Brad Ackerman

characters.description: The twelve-year-old youngest stepbrother, whose enthusiasm for research and local history makes him unexpectedly useful. Suze calls him Doc.
characters.name: David Ackerman

characters.description: Suze's friend and classmate, a school-paper writer with albinism who can find anything in an archive and enjoys doing it. She helps trace the history of the family who once owned the land the Ackermans live on.
characters.name: CeeCee Webb

characters.description: CeeCee's inseparable friend and Suze's, good-humored and usually driving.
characters.name: Adam McTavish

recaps.ending: Jesse's remains are found in the Ackermans' backyard and given a proper burial, and the murder that kept him here is finally uncovered: Maria de Silva, who did not want to marry the cousin she was engaged to, had Felix Diego kill him in the boarding house that became Suze's home, and the two spent a century and a half keeping it quiet. Maria and Diego are driven off for good, and Suze is seriously hurt doing it. With his death accounted for and his body at rest, nothing is holding Jesse here, and Suze has to face losing him. He does not go. Jesse chooses to stay, and the reason is Suze, which neither of them knows what to do with, and which changes nothing about the fact that one of them is dead. Jack Slater leaves at the end of the summer no longer frightened of what he can see and knowing he is not the only one. Paul Slater leaves too, making it clear he intends to come back, and that he knows a great deal more about what people like them can do than Father Dominic has ever told her.
recaps.in_short: Suze takes a summer job minding Jack Slater, a frightened boy staying at a Pebble Beach resort, and quickly realizes he sees the dead as she does. His older brother Paul does too, calls people like them shifters rather than mediators, and claims to know far more about the ability than Father Dominic. Meanwhile Suze's stepfather starts excavating the backyard for a hot tub, and the ghost of Maria de Silva, a nineteenth-century woman engaged to her cousin Hector, appears to demand the digging stop. Research reveals that Hector, who supposedly vanished in 1850, is Jesse: he was murdered in the house on Maria's orders by Felix Diego, the man she married instead, and buried in the yard. Maria and Diego attack to keep it hidden, and Suze is badly hurt driving them out. Jesse's remains are found and buried properly, freeing him to move on, and he stays instead, for Suze. Paul leaves promising to return.

recaps.text: Susannah Simon is a mediator: she sees and speaks with the dead, who come to her to have whatever holds them here finished, and she has kept it from her family her whole life. Her mother's remarriage moved her from Brooklyn to Carmel-by-the-Sea, into a house her stepfather Andy is restoring, with three stepbrothers she privately calls Sleepy, Dopey and Doc. Her bedroom came with Jesse, the ghost of a young man who died in that room in the nineteenth century and has never said why he stayed; over a year he has become the person she tells the truth to, and neither of them will name what else he has become. At the Junipero Serra Mission Academy the principal, Father Dominic, turned out to be a mediator as well, and the two work together while disagreeing about method: he counsels the dead, she fights them. Suze has driven a violent ghost out of the school, carried a dead woman's message into a wealthy family's affairs, and stopped four dead teenagers from killing the boy they blamed for their crash, learning afterward that he had earned their anger.

Summer in Carmel, and Suze needs a job. She is hired to look after Jack Slater, a young boy staying with his family at a Pebble Beach resort, and finds him exhausted, withdrawn and terrified. It takes her very little time to work out why: Jack sees the dead exactly as she does, has no idea what he is, and has been treated by the adults around him as a problem to be managed. His older brother Paul is charming, attentive and openly interested in Suze. At home, Andy has decided the backyard needs a hot tub, which means digging up ground that has been undisturbed since the house was built.

Suze begins teaching Jack what she knows, against the wishes of his parents, who would rather he stopped talking about it. Paul encourages her, then tells her why: he sees the dead too. He calls people like them shifters rather than mediators and claims to know far more about what they can do than Father Dominic has ever admitted to. Meanwhile a ghost arrives at the Ackerman house: Maria de Silva, a young woman from an old Californian family, dressed for the middle of the nineteenth century, who orders Suze to stop the excavation in the backyard and threatens her when she refuses. With CeeCee's help Suze traces the family history and finds that Maria was engaged to her own cousin, Hector de Silva, who disappeared in 1850 on his way to marry her and was assumed to have run off. The portrait that comes with the story is unmistakably Jesse.

Jesse never ran. He was killed in the boarding house that later became the Ackermans' home, and buried in the yard Andy is about to dig up, which is why Maria wants the work stopped. Suze keeps as much of this from Jesse as she can while she works out the rest of it, and finds that Maria is not acting alone: Felix Diego, the man Maria married after her cousin vanished, is with her, and he is the one who does the harm. The threats become attacks. Suze's work with Jack continues alongside it, and Paul's interest in her sharpens as he realizes how little she knows about what they are. The excavation goes ahead on schedule.

The confrontation comes at the house, and it is the most dangerous fight Suze has been in. The whole of it comes out: Maria had no intention of marrying a cousin she did not want, arranged for Diego to kill him in that room, and the two of them have spent a century and a half making sure nobody found the body. Jesse, who never understood why he could not leave, hears it from the people who killed him. Suze is seriously injured before it ends, but Maria and Diego are driven off for good, and the bones in the backyard are uncovered.

Jesse's remains are given a proper burial, and with his murder accounted for and his body at rest there is nothing left to hold him here. Suze spends the end of the book expecting to lose him. He does not go: Jesse chooses to stay, and the reason is her, which neither of them has any idea what to do with and which does not change the fact that one of them is dead. Suze recovers from her injuries with the usual explanations at home. Jack leaves with his family at the end of the summer, steadier than he arrived and no longer believing he is the only one. Paul goes with them, promising to be back, and leaves Suze with the knowledge that he understands what they can do far better than Father Dominic ever has.

characters.description: The daughter of Lord Sezu of the Acoma, seventeen years old and days away from taking final vows as a novice in the temple of Lashima. She is intelligent, stubborn and entirely untrained in politics, having chosen the contemplative life precisely to avoid the endless manoeuvring of the Tsurani nobility. Word from the war beyond the rift takes that choice away from her and leaves her the head of a great house that has just been reduced to almost nothing.
characters.name: Mara of the Acoma

characters.description: Mara's childhood nurse, an old woman of the Acoma household who has served the family all her life. Blunt, superstitious, sharp about people, and unafraid to tell her mistress uncomfortable truths, she becomes the closest thing the ruined house has to a political adviser.
characters.name: Nacoya

characters.description: Force Commander of the Acoma, a scarred veteran of many campaigns who has served the family since Mara's father was a boy. Utterly correct in manner, he is one of the very few survivors of the disaster that killed his lord, and he holds himself responsible for a house he can no longer defend.
characters.name: Keyoke

characters.description: A Strike Leader of the Acoma and Keyoke's constant shadow, a large, silent soldier of exceptional skill. He is the officer entrusted with Mara's personal safety, and his loyalty to the house is absolute even when the honour code he lives by turns against him.
characters.name: Papewaio

characters.description: Lord of the Minwanabi, master of one of the Empire's five greatest houses and the hereditary enemy of the Acoma. Powerful, well allied and confident, he arranged the deaths that left the Acoma leaderless and intends to finish the family without ever appearing to have broken the forms of honour.
characters.name: Jingu of the Minwanabi

characters.description: The Acoma hadonra, the estate's manager, a small anxious man responsible for its accounts, herds, workers and trade. He is scrupulously honest and permanently alarmed by his new mistress's willingness to spend money on things no Tsurani noble would spend money on.
characters.name: Jican

characters.description: Lord of the Anasati, head of another of the Empire's great houses, an old rival of Mara's father and currently allied with the Minwanabi. He is a careful, intelligent player of the Game of the Council who prefers advantage to bloodshed and dislikes being manoeuvred.
characters.name: Tecuma of the Anasati

characters.description: The second son of the Lord of the Anasati, thickset, loud and physical, with a taste for wrestling, drink and the pleasure houses of the city. His father regards him as the least gifted of his sons, and he knows it.
characters.name: Buntokapi

characters.description: The eldest son and heir of the Lord of the Anasati, clever, cold and well aware of his own quality. He takes an interest in Mara and does not take being passed over gracefully.
characters.name: Jiro of the Anasati

characters.description: A grey warrior, one of the masterless soldiers whose lord was destroyed and who are held by Tsurani custom to have lost all honour and all place in the world. Cheerful, quick-tongued and a gifted officer, he is a distant cousin of the Acoma and is offered something no grey warrior is ever offered.
characters.name: Lujan

characters.description: Former Spy Master of a house destroyed in the Game of the Council, who kept his network alive after his master's death with no one left to serve. Unremarkable to look at and able to pass as anything from a labourer to a priest, he offers his organisation to the one ruler who might survive long enough to use it.
characters.name: Arakasi

characters.description: A younger son of the Lord of the Shinzawai, a northern house that keeps out of the Minwanabi quarrel. Courteous, observant and noticeably more thoughtful than the other young nobles Mara meets, he treats her as a person rather than as a piece on a board.
characters.name: Hokanu of the Shinzawai

characters.description: The ruler of a hive of the cho-ja, the insectoid people who live alongside humans on Kelewan and whose warriors, silk and craftsmen are prized by every great house. A new queen bargains for the land her hive will settle on, and negotiates on terms most Tsurani nobles are too proud to learn.
characters.name: The cho-ja Queen

characters.description: A courtesan of striking beauty and expensive tastes, ambitious far beyond the position her trade allows and skilled at making herself indispensable to powerful men. Her charm is entirely deliberate and her temper, when it slips, is vicious.
characters.name: Teani

characters.description: Mara's infant son, heir to the Acoma and, through his father, grandson of the Lord of the Anasati. His birth alters the balance between the two houses, because a family that would happily see the Acoma destroyed cannot afford to see its own blood destroyed with it.
characters.name: Ayaki

characters.description: The Warlord of Tsuranuanni, holder of the white and gold, the most powerful man in the Empire after the Light of Heaven himself. He commands the war on the barbarian world, uses it to keep rival houses obedient and bled, and enjoys his own supremacy openly.
characters.name: Warlord Almecho

recaps.ending: Mara survives the Minwanabi trap and turns it. Attending the Warlord's celebration at Lord Jingu's own estate, protected only by the guest-right that Tsurani custom makes absolute, she is hunted through the house by his agents; Papewaio is killed defending her. Rather than fleeing, Mara forces the matter into the open in front of the Warlord and the assembled nobility, and demonstrates that Jingu attempted murder under his own roof. The dishonour is total and public, and Jingu takes his own life. His son Desio inherits the Minwanabi with their alliances weakened and their standing damaged, and swears a blood oath to his god that he will destroy the Acoma. Mara goes home the acknowledged victor of the season's Game. In one year she has taken a house of a few dozen soldiers and rebuilt it into a power with thousands of men, a cho-ja hive, an intelligence network under Arakasi, and a reputation nobody expected. She rules for her infant son Ayaki, whose Anasati blood obliges Lord Tecuma to protect him even though Tecuma will never forgive her for his son's death. The war beyond the rift continues, the Warlord's grip on the Empire is unchallenged, and the feud that has consumed both houses for generations is not over. The story continues in Servant of the Empire.
recaps.in_short: Mara, seventeen and about to take vows as a temple novice, is called home when her father and brother are killed on the barbarian world in a battle engineered by the Minwanabi, leaving her Ruling Lady of a house reduced to a handful of soldiers. Guided by her old nurse Nacoya and her Force Commander Keyoke, she rebuilds by breaking Tsurani convention: she recruits masterless grey warriors, bargains with a cho-ja queen for a hive on Acoma land, and takes the spymaster Arakasi into her service. To gain protection she marries Buntokapi, the least promising son of the Anasati, so his family must defend her house, then manoeuvres him into a position where honour leaves him no choice but to take his own life, leaving her ruling for their infant son. Finally she attends the Warlord's celebration at the Minwanabi estate, where her enemy Lord Jingu means to kill her without breaking guest-right. Papewaio dies protecting her, but Mara exposes Jingu's treachery before the Empire and he is forced to take his own life, leaving his son Desio sworn to destroy her.

recaps.text: This book runs alongside the Riftwar Saga and tells the story from the other side of the rift, on the world of Kelewan. What a reader needs going in is the setting rather than any earlier plot. Kelewan is ruled by the Empire of Tsuranuanni, a rigid, ancient society in which honour is public, absolute and more valuable than life, and in which suicide is an accepted answer to disgrace. Below the Emperor, called the Light of Heaven and treated as a religious figure rather than a governing one, real power belongs to the Warlord and to the great houses, who compete endlessly for position in what they call the Game of the Council: a contest fought with marriages, trade, assassination and manufactured accidents, in which whole families are erased and the winners are congratulated. Above the law entirely stands the Assembly of Magicians, the Great Ones, who answer to no lord. For some years the Empire has been fighting a war on another world, reached through a magical rift and inhabited by people the Tsurani call barbarians. The Warlord runs that war, and the great houses send their sons and their armies to it, knowing that it is being used to raise some families and bleed others.

Mara, seventeen, is pulled out of the temple of Lashima on the morning she is to take her final vows: her father, Lord Sezu of the Acoma, and her brother Lanokota are dead on the barbarian world, killed in a battle deliberately arranged to expose them. She is now Ruling Lady of the Acoma, a great house reduced to a name, an estate and a few dozen soldiers, with almost all of its strength buried on another world. Her enemy is Lord Jingu of the Minwanabi, whose family has been at feud with hers for generations and who intends to finish the work this season. Her assets are an old nurse, Nacoya, who becomes her adviser, a Force Commander, Keyoke, who is one of the few survivors, and the soldier Papewaio. Everyone expects her to be dead or married off within months. Mara, who has no training in politics whatever, decides to play the Game of the Council instead.

Mara begins by doing things no Tsurani ruler would consider. She sends Keyoke to make contact with grey warriors, the masterless soldiers whose lords were destroyed and who are held to have lost all honour and all place in the world, and offers them service under the Acoma: hundreds accept, among them a quick-witted distant cousin named Lujan, and the house's strength grows in secret. When Papewaio is caught by the letter of the honour code and condemned to die for an act that saved her, she circumvents the sentence by declaring the condemned man's black headband the badge of a new honour guard rather than a mark of death. She also opens negotiations with a young cho-ja queen for a hive to be founded on Acoma land, bargaining for warriors, silk and craftsmen, and paying in courtesy that other nobles are too proud to offer.

Strength alone will not save the Acoma from the Minwanabi, so Mara buys protection with a marriage. She approaches Lord Tecuma of the Anasati, her father's old rival and Jingu's ally, and asks for one of his sons, then deliberately chooses Buntokapi, the coarse and slow-witted second son whom Tecuma values least. The bargain works exactly as intended: with Anasati blood ruling the Acoma, the Anasati must defend the house they had been helping to destroy, and Jingu's alliance is broken. The price is that Buntokapi becomes Ruling Lord and Mara becomes a subordinate wife in her own house, subject to a husband who is loud, violent-tempered and pleased with his new power. She endures him, bears him a son, Ayaki, and waits. During this period Arakasi, the surviving Spy Master of a house destroyed years earlier, brings her his intact intelligence network and enters Acoma service.

Buntokapi rules badly and hates the paperwork, so Mara encourages the parts of his character that will get him out of the way: she buys him a town house in Sulan-Qu, where the wrestling matches and the gambling are, and where a beautiful and ambitious courtesan named Teani makes herself indispensable to him. To keep the estate running in his absence he grants his wife written authority to act in his name. Mara uses it. Acting with her husband's seal she manoeuvres the Acoma into positions that damage the Minwanabi and set the house at odds with the Warlord's interests, decisions Buntokapi would never have permitted and which, once made, cannot be unmade. She then arranges for him to discover exactly what has been done in his name, at a moment of her choosing rather than his.

Buntokapi comes home and learns everything, and finds that Tsurani honour has closed every exit. He can kill his wife, but that would put his infant son under Anasati regency and hand the Acoma to his own father, ending the house's independence and his own standing with it; he cannot disown decisions taken lawfully under his own authority; and he cannot outmanoeuvre the woman who arranged the position. He takes his own life by the sword, in the correct form, and dies as Lord of the Acoma. Mara is Ruling Lady again, with Ayaki as her heir. Lord Tecuma understands perfectly what has been done to his son and will never forgive her, but Ayaki is his grandson and Anasati blood, so he must go on protecting the house that killed Buntokapi. The Acoma have survived the year, and the Minwanabi have lost their ally.

Mara is summoned to a celebration for the Warlord held at Lord Jingu's own lake estate, an invitation she cannot refuse and which Jingu intends to be her last journey. Under Tsurani custom a guest cannot be harmed by her host, so Jingu's plan is to have her killed in a way that cannot be traced to him, and the household is full of his agents. Mara arrives with a small guard and spends the visit under continuous attack. Papewaio is killed defending her. Rather than run, she forces the matter into the open before the Warlord and the assembled nobility of the Empire and proves that murder was attempted under Jingu's roof. The disgrace is absolute and public, and Jingu takes his own life to spare his family total ruin. His son Desio inherits a damaged house and swears a blood oath to destroy the Acoma. Mara goes home the season's clear victor, ruling for her son, with an army, a cho-ja hive and a spy network she did not have a year earlier.

characters.description: A seven-year-old child of Feylon nearing his first tiering. He plans to claim an imperial tithe, serve one year in the army, and then return to help his village.
characters.name: Jiran

characters.description: Feylon's only tier-four hunter.
characters.name: Skandor

characters.description: Jiran's tier-three uncle, a former army soldier who runs Feylon's courier shop and can use a spear technique.
characters.name: Jiran's uncle

characters.description: Jiran's father, who supports a plan to prepare his son for army service through spear and hunter training.
characters.name: Jiran's father

characters.description: Jiran's mother, who joins his father in setting a training plan to prepare their son for army service.
characters.name: Jiran's mother

characters.description: Jiran's tier-one cousin, one season older than him and the daughter of his uncle. She protects Jiran from hostile apprentices by invoking imperial law.
characters.name: Niya

characters.description: An unidentified high-tier noble who seeks someone at Jiran's uncle's courier shop. His mind-affecting whisper incapacitates Niya, but Jiran resists it.
characters.name: Unidentified noble

characters.description: The newly installed provincial magistrate and the powerful noble previously encountered at Jiran's uncle's shop. He protects Jiran from immediate danger, expands the uncle's courier duties, and takes a particular interest in Jiran's condition.
characters.name: Feylon Samris

characters.description: A seamstress whose family gathers eggs along the cove ridges. She arrives with several workers and a cart of provisions for Samris's manor, helping establish the household where Jiran will live under the magistrate's protection.
characters.name: Sharel

characters.description: A deceased man from Earth whose memories remain accessible to Jiran after the failed tiering. Those memories give Jiran a store of advanced scientific ideas, which he begins preserving in coded form as recalling them becomes easier.
characters.name: Brandon

characters.description: An elderly noble who reveals that he has been listening after Jiran reports a new way to absorb the chaotic density of Densoon.
characters.name: Elderly noble

characters.description: An elderly noble who tests Jiran's judgment and accepts him as a mentee. He makes the search for hidden truths a condition of their relationship and refuses to permit Jiran's next tier until the boy achieves two-way communication with mana.
characters.name: Lenton

characters.description: An assassin who arranged a trap for several gifted children. Their implanted escape talismans deliver them into his custody after shadow-like attackers overwhelm their protector, and he takes them away under the claim that they are going to a new home.
characters.name: Markhiss

characters.description: One of the gifted children caught in a mausoleum trap with two companions. He uses an implanted escape talisman when shadow-like attackers overwhelm the group's sworn protector, only to discover that the device has delivered him into Markhiss's custody.
characters.name: Dommell

characters.description: A noble child held by Markhiss alongside Dommell and another captive. After being transported to a coastal forest, she is coerced into promising obedience and witnesses the power of the person controlling them.
characters.name: Oliviala LeCruex

characters.description: Oliviala LeCruex's cousin and a fellow prisoner of Markhiss. He is brought with her and Dommell to a decayed inland village, then confined in a cramped blue-metal cage that rapidly drains their mana and leaves all three children powerless.
characters.name: Cameron

characters.description: A powerful crowned man who arrives after the hidden settlement's barrier falls. He checks on Olive, prompts Markhiss to withdraw, and is addressed by Lenton as emperor.
characters.name: Emperor

recaps.ending: Jiran enters Markhiss's concealed settlement as a prisoner but learns to resist and drain its mana-siphoning restraints. He kills two tier-four bandits, refuses to stand aside when Markhiss orders Dommell's execution, and turns the cage's stored power against the settlement. The cage disintegrates, leaving Oliviala LeCruex, Dommell, and the third captive free but unconscious, while Jiran's attack destroys the barrier hiding the settlement. Markhiss remains unharmed and withdraws when a far stronger crowned emperor arrives. Lenton follows, identifies Jiran to the emperor as his disciple, and renders the injured, depleted boy unconscious. Jiran has survived at tier two with above-cap attributes, Foresight, several elemental techniques, and an active Challenger timer, but the origin and cost of these changes remain unknown. His father has begun repairing their relationship, while his mother remains estranged. Niya continues training with Samris. Markhiss escapes, the captives' recovery is not shown, and Jiran still owes army service. The ancient cube, the nature of density, Brandon's memories, Jiran's neural changes, and the curses shared by the Unique ascenders all remain unresolved.
recaps.in_short: After a disastrous first tiering leaves seven-year-old Jiran scarred, rejected by his family, and carrying memories from a dead man on Earth, the new magistrate Samris shelters and trains him. Jiran heals, develops unconventional mana control, and becomes the pupil of Lenton, another powerful ascender with a Unique curse. At tier two, Jiran gains healing and elemental techniques, discovers that his danger sense is Foresight, and acquires Challenger Density, which rewards difficult kills while feeding a dangerous urge for violence. He teaches Niya direct mana conversion, exceeds normal tier limits, and investigates an ancient elemental cube. A wilderness trial eventually leads him underground and into Markhiss's hidden slaver settlement, where Oliviala LeCruex, Dommell, and another child are imprisoned. Jiran defeats two stronger bandits, drains the captives' cage, frees them, and destroys the barrier concealing the settlement. Markhiss escapes when the emperor arrives. Lenton claims the exhausted Jiran as his disciple, but the captives' recovery and the mysteries surrounding Jiran's powers remain open.

recaps.text: Jiran, a seven-year-old child of Feylon, reaches the threshold for his first tier and claims an imperial share of a fourth-tier beast killed by Skandor and his uncle. Shame over taking the meat prompts him to double his future military pledge, binding him to fourteen seasons of service. During the tiering ceremony, his mana vanishes into an anomaly near his neck and memories from a dead adult on Earth enter his mind. His body cracks, but he discovers that he can convert ambient density and direct mana to repair himself. His mother, convinced he may become a feral threat, attempts to kill him before his father intervenes. Jiran escapes as priests approach. Niya protects him from village apprentices, and an unknown noble proves unable to control him with a mind-affecting whisper. The noble summons the elders, protects Jiran, and is revealed as Feylon Samris, the new magistrate. Jiran's uncle gives him shelter, then Samris offers him protected employment as a manor squire through his third birthing celebration. Jiran accepts, moves into the manor, meets Sharel, and prepares for Samris to investigate his unusual condition.

Samris determines that a serious injury has been consuming nearly all of Jiran's density and mana. With dense food, exercise, study, and careful observation, Jiran repairs the damage and can retain mana again. He conceals how readily he can convert density and guide mana, while his access to Brandon's scientific memories improves. Choosing a combat path, Jiran faces a tier-two crab and discovers Forcing, a mana-driven movement technique. Samris shifts him toward practical spear training and controlled combat, worried that conventional instruction might restrict his unusual development. Jiran learns rapidly but repeatedly injures himself by pushing beyond safe limits. He kills a boar, defines protection as his reason for using lethal force, then nearly dies fighting a group of same-tier creatures before Samris rescues him. Samris warns him to report any danger intuition or altered perception that might signal an awakening Unique ability. When Densoon begins, chaotic waves of density injure Jiran even as his Molding reaches level fifty. He must choose among permanent subskills while Samris is briefly away, and he remains uncertain how to balance his emotion-based control with sound judgment.

Jiran selects Mana Expansion and learns to extend mana beyond his body. Under Samris's supervision he combines that control with Forcing, develops protective mana techniques, and survives increasingly difficult beast fights. He also learns to absorb the chaotic density of Densoon by matching its motion. After reaching the limits of tier one, he is forbidden to ascend until an elderly noble named Lenton evaluates him. Lenton accepts Jiran as a mentee devoted to investigating density's hidden nature, but demands that he achieve two-way communication with mana first. Jiran eventually receives a confusing response from an unidentified presence and unlocks Revelation. Lenton explains that he, Samris, and Jiran possess Unique abilities outside ordinary progression and that each such ability carries a curse. He hopes Jiran can help investigate those curses. Lenton then begins Jiran's tier-two ascent with powerful pills and a filter intended to remove impurities from his mana body. During the transformation, Jiran encounters a pale-blue, star-like presence before losing consciousness.

Jiran completes his ascent to tier two and gains Shaping, but his scientific approach makes even tiny elemental experiments dangerously powerful. He develops regeneration and lightning control, then uses lightning to defend Feylon from a crab attack. He kills a tier-four mutant and absorbs crimson density that brings euphoria and a compulsion to kill. His father apologizes for abandoning him, beginning a reconciliation, though Jiran's mother remains committed to Church teaching and unforgiven. Jiran's status reveals Challenger Density and a countdown he fears may be fatal. He cannot speak or write about it because an outside force blocks every attempt. Niya asks him to help her grow stronger, and Lenton makes Jiran his apprentice while allowing him to train her. Meanwhile, an ancient cube responds to Jiran's controlled fire. Markhiss transports Oliviala LeCruex, Dommell, and another captive to a coastal forest, coerces their obedience, and demonstrates overwhelming firepower. Their captivity continues while Jiran remains isolated in his search for the meaning of the Challenger timer.

After Jiran shares dangerous mana knowledge with Niya, Lenton removes both children from Feylon. Jiran is sent alone across plains while his Challenger timer falls toward expiration. Surrounded by tier-four beasts, he combines fire, gas, ice, and light to survive. Personal kills release more crimson density, extend the timer, and push his growth and attributes beyond their normal tier-two limits. His recurring danger warning is finally identified as Foresight. Jiran delays his next ascent to test these gains, reunites with Samris and Niya, and learns that Lenton's own Unique curse forces him to repay value received. Lenton also helps him understand that direct density conversion could destabilize the Empire's religious and political teachings. Jiran continues opening the ancient cube with multiple elements and develops adaptive elemental protection. In the parallel captivity, Oliviala LeCruex, her cousin Cameron, and Dommell are brought to a decayed settlement under Markhiss's control. He locks them in a cramped metal cage that drains their mana. The children are left hungry and weak, while Olive tries to preserve their discipline and judgment. A vast dome briefly appears over the surrounding area, but its purpose remains unclear.

Lenton sends Jiran against a displaced hive threatening coastal settlements. Jiran destroys many creatures but recognizes that Challenger Density is intensifying his desire to kill. Lenton warns that ascenders can lose themselves to slaughter and advises Jiran to delay tier three until his judgment is steadier. Further work on the ancient cube coincides with unexplained neural changes, including Active Dual Mind, which lets Jiran manage several elemental effects at once. He refuses an offer to disable these limit-breaking changes despite warnings of brain damage or psychosis. While testing an explosive fireball against a mutated tier-four beast, Jiran is badly injured and falls into underground tunnels. He restores himself, finds a strange vine carrying Densoon density, and fights insects and light-sensitive shadow creatures while seeking an exit. Lenton deliberately leaves him to escape without rescue after recognizing that constant protection has encouraged recklessness. Jiran reaches an abandoned mine shaft and launches himself toward the surface with almost no mana left. A waiting captor knocks him down and locks a mana-draining collar around his neck. Markhiss tells Olive's group that the underground intruder will soon be brought to their cage.

Jiran learns to halt the collar's drain, siphon its stored mana, and restore himself. Taken into a concealed slaver settlement, he chooses to investigate the other prisoners before escaping. He finds Oliviala LeCruex, Dommell, and a third captive inside a mana-draining cage. Jiran kills a tier-four slaver with ice and destroys his own collar, but the prisoners initially refuse freedom because Olive believes obedience to their coerced promise offers protection. Markhiss arrives and is revealed as the settlement's tier-six leader, hidden behind an obfuscation barrier. When he orders Dommell hanged, Jiran resists despite knowing he cannot defeat Markhiss directly. Jiran kills another tier-four bandit, drains the cage, and uses its stored mana for a large attack above the settlement. The cage disintegrates, freeing the unconscious captives, and the blast destroys the barrier that kept the settlement hidden. Markhiss survives unharmed and leaves when a vastly stronger crowned emperor arrives. Lenton appears, addresses the newcomer as emperor, identifies Jiran as his disciple, and renders the exhausted boy unconscious. The settlement is exposed, but Markhiss remains at large and the immediate recovery of Jiran and the other captives is not shown.

characters.description: A young Thaylen merchant and ship-owner, once apprentice to a shrewd master trader, now adapting to a life reshaped by a fall that left her unable to use her legs. Practical, observant, and quietly ambitious, she keeps a rare exotic pet and is learning to lead rather than merely follow, weighing profit against the harder questions of duty.
characters.name: Rysn

characters.description: An irrepressibly cheerful Herdazian soldier of Bridge Four who became a Windrunner, able to draw on the storms to fly and to heal. Famous for his boasts, his jokes, and his enormous family, he masks a genuine, fierce loyalty and a surprising depth of heart beneath the constant comedy.
characters.name: Lopen

characters.description: Rysn's beloved pet, a rare winged creature that feeds on the light of the storms and behaves something like a cross between an insect and a small, affectionate animal. Rysn dotes on it, and it seems to be more unusual than even she realizes.
characters.name: Chiri-Chiri

characters.description: A Horneater woman, daughter of one of Bridge Four's own, who has taken up a recovered suit of ancient warrior's armor and fights as a skilled archer. Cheerful and matter-of-fact about her people's beliefs, she brings both firepower and an outsider's clear eye to the expedition.
characters.name: Cord

characters.description: A member of the expedition's crew who proves to be far more than a simple laborer: a guardian bound to keep an ancient and dangerous secret buried. Watchful and evasive, it acts to prevent the travelers from uncovering something it believes must never fall into the wrong hands.
characters.name: Nikli

recaps.ending: The expedition reaches the guarded island and uncovers its true secret: it hides one of the Dawnshards, ancient powers of pure Command that predate even the world's gods and could reshape reality in the wrong hands. A trusted member of the crew is exposed as a guardian devoted to keeping that secret hidden, and it moves to stop the travelers from carrying the knowledge back, terrified that the enemy god Odium could claim such a power. In the confrontation the Windrunner Lopen speaks a further oath and comes into greater strength. Rather than let the Dawnshard be lost or seized, Rysn accepts it into herself, becoming its living vessel and secret keeper, a role that changes her forever and binds her exotic pet's fate to the island's mysteries as well. The expedition survives and sails home. Rysn returns transformed, now the quiet guardian of one of the most dangerous forces in the cosmos, understanding that the war against Odium has stakes far larger than any single kingdom, and that the enemy hunts for exactly what she now carries.
recaps.in_short: The Thaylen merchant Rysn is commissioned to lead an expedition to a forbidden, supposedly dead island wrapped in legend, to learn what secret it hides. She sails with a wary ship's crew and a guard of Radiants, including the Windrunner Lopen and the archer Cord, past natural hazards and stranger defenses. Breaching the island, they discover it conceals one of the Dawnshards, primal powers of Command older and more fundamental than the gods that shape the world. A member of the crew is revealed as a hidden guardian sworn to keep the secret buried and to stop them from exposing it, fearing the enemy god could seize it. In the crisis Lopen deepens his own oaths, and Rysn makes a fateful choice: she takes the Dawnshard into herself, becoming its new secret bearer and protector. The expedition survives and returns, and Rysn quietly carries one of the most dangerous powers in existence, aware that the enemy is searching for it.

recaps.text: Before this story: On the world of Roshar an ancient enemy has returned, and the god of hatred, Odium, wages war on humanity through immortal warriors and awakened armies. A coalition of nations, led by the Kholin family from the recovered mountain city of Urithiru, has begun to reunite the world and to restore the long-lost Knights Radiant, whose members again draw power from the great storms to fly, heal, and fight. The wealthy trading nation of Thaylenah, having survived a devastating assault, is a key part of that alliance. Amid these vast events, a young Thaylen merchant named Rysn, trained under a shrewd master trader and adjusting to life after an injury that cost her the use of her legs, keeps up her trade and cares for a rare, storm-fed pet. When a powerful patron seeks someone discreet and capable to investigate a forbidden island long shrouded in legend, Rysn's path turns from ordinary commerce toward a secret with consequences for the whole world.

Rysn is entrusted with leading an expedition to a distant, forbidden island that most believe is dead and cursed, in order to discover the truth hidden there. A ship is prepared and a crew assembled, including a guard of Knights Radiant among them the cheerful Windrunner Lopen and the Horneater archer Cord, to protect the venture from whatever waits at their destination. The voyage tests them with hard weather and the ship crew's uneasy superstitions about where they are bound, and Rysn must grow into command over sailors who did not choose her and who fear the island's reputation. As they draw closer, it becomes clear that the island is not simply abandoned but actively guarded, and that reaching whatever it conceals will demand more than seamanship. Strange signs and dangers gather around the approach.

The expedition breaks through the island's defenses and finds the secret at its heart: it shelters one of the Dawnshards, a primal power of Command older and more fundamental than the world's gods, capable of catastrophic misuse. A member of the crew is revealed as a hidden guardian sworn to keep that power buried, and it acts to prevent the travelers from exposing it, dreading that the enemy god could seize such a force. In the crisis the Windrunner Lopen speaks a deeper oath and grows stronger. Faced with letting the Dawnshard be lost or taken, Rysn chooses to accept it into herself, becoming its living vessel and secret keeper, a choice that transforms her and entangles her exotic pet in the island's mysteries. The travelers survive and sail home. Rysn returns changed, now the quiet guardian of one of the most dangerous powers in existence, aware that the enemy is hunting for precisely what she now carries.

characters.description: A telepathic waitress at Merlotte's bar in Bon Temps, Louisiana. She has accepted that she is part fairy, descended from the prince Niall Brigant, and she is spared by the new Nevada regime because her mind-reading makes her useful. She is bonded to the vampire Eric Northman by exchanged blood, estranged from Bill Compton since learning he was ordered to seduce her, and quietly building a relationship with Hunter, the small telepathic son of her dead cousin.
characters.name: Sookie Stackhouse

characters.description: The owner of Merlotte's, a shapeshifter and Sookie's employer of many years. Cautious by temperament, he has kept what he is hidden from the town for his whole adult life, and the decision facing every two-natured person in the world falls hardest on someone whose livelihood depends on Bon Temps liking him.
characters.name: Sam Merlotte

characters.description: The Viking vampire who owns Fangtasia and holds Shreveport and its territory as sheriff, now serving Felipe de Castro of Nevada with a regent set over him. He and Sookie share a blood bond and an unresolved attachment, and he is increasingly concerned that the new king's people will decide to claim Sookie outright.
characters.name: Eric Northman

characters.description: Sookie's vampire neighbor and former lover, now permanently out of favor after she learned he was sent to Bon Temps under the old queen's orders to attach himself to her. He keeps to his house across the cemetery, works on his vampire database, and has never stopped watching out for her whether she wants it or not.
characters.name: Bill Compton

characters.description: Sookie's brother, a werepanther by infection rather than birth, married to Crystal Norris of Hotshot. The marriage is unhappy and unfaithful on both sides and is common knowledge in two communities, which does nothing for his standing with the panthers or with his sister.
characters.name: Jason Stackhouse

characters.description: A New Orleans witch lodging in Sookie's upstairs rooms since the hurricane, capable, loud, and not always careful. She is the closest thing Sookie has to a female friend in the house and provides most of its magical defenses.
characters.name: Amelia Broadway

characters.description: Jason's wife, a werepanther born in the inbred, insular community at Hotshot. She is pregnant, restless, and openly unfaithful, and her behavior has strained relations between Jason and the panthers who consider her theirs.
characters.name: Crystal Norris

characters.description: A werepanther from Hotshot and one of Jason's regular drinking companions, a quiet man who keeps his distance from the rest of the panther community and seems more comfortable in Jason's company than in his own family's.
characters.name: Mel Hart

characters.description: Sookie's fairy godmother, a full-blooded fairy of Niall's line who has appeared throughout Sookie's life to pull her out of danger. She is pregnant, which for a fairy is rare and precious, and she is more anxious than usual about what her own people are doing.
characters.name: Claudine Crane

characters.description: Sookie's great-grandfather, prince of the fairies, ancient and courtly. He visits her when it suits him, deflects her questions about fairy politics, and is plainly managing a conflict among his own kind that he does not want to describe to her.
characters.name: Niall Brigant

characters.description: A Shreveport werewolf and locksmith, blunt and competent, who has done security work for Sookie's household before. He is trusted enough by both wolves and vampires to be hired as a bodyguard when Sookie's house needs guarding.
characters.name: Tray Dawson

characters.description: A fairy who looks almost exactly like Jason Stackhouse and turns out to be a relative, Niall's son and therefore Sookie's great-uncle. His behavior is erratic and his loyalties are impossible to read, and Niall speaks of him with a mixture of grief and warning.
characters.name: Dermot Brigant

characters.description: A fairy noble who leads the faction opposing Niall Brigant. He wants the fae to sever every remaining tie with the human world, and he regards Niall's human-blooded descendants as the tie most worth cutting.
characters.name: Breandan

characters.description: A fairy in Breandan's service, beautiful and entirely without pity, who works alongside Lochlan. The pair are known among their own people for taking a craftsman's interest in the suffering of others.
characters.name: Neave

characters.description: A fairy in Breandan's service and Neave's inseparable partner, sharing her tastes and her reputation. Where she is theatrical he is methodical, and neither is deterred by anything a captive says.
characters.name: Lochlan

characters.description: A vampire made by the same maker as Bill Compton, and therefore his sister in blood, living well away from Louisiana. Their shared history is long and painful, and she has kept her distance from him for years.
characters.name: Judith Vardamme

recaps.ending: The fairy war ends with Sookie's rescue and Niall's victory, both paid for heavily. Bill kills Neave and Eric kills Lochlan, but the fairies' blood is poison to vampires and Bill is left dying of it; he survives only because Sookie has Eric find Judith Vardamme, his sister in blood, whose blood heals him. Niall kills Breandan, then tells Sookie that the only way to stop the killing for good is to shut Faery, and closes the doors between the worlds behind him. Sookie loses her fairy godmother Claudine and her bodyguard Tray Dawson in the fighting, and is left physically maimed and badly traumatized by her captivity. Claude and Dermot are among the part-fairies stranded on the human side. In Bon Temps, Mel Hart is exposed as the man responsible for Crystal's death, and the Hotshot panthers deal with him under their own law rather than the state's. Jason is cleared and widowed. Eric's marriage to Sookie by vampire custom stands, which shields her from Felipe de Castro and Victor Madden but binds her further into vampire politics. The two-natured are now public, permanently, and Bon Temps has to decide what it thinks of that.
recaps.in_short: The world's shapeshifters and werewolves announce their existence on television, and Sam Merlotte changes shape in front of his own customers. Days later Jason's pregnant wife Crystal is found crucified in the bar's parking lot, and the search for her killer runs through the whole book alongside a far larger danger: a faction of fairies led by Breandan wants every human-blooded descendant of Prince Niall Brigant dead, and Sookie is at the top of the list. Eric marries Sookie by vampire custom to keep her out of the new Nevada regime's hands, and guards are posted around her home, but the fairies kill her protectors one by one, including her fairy godmother Claudine and the werewolf Tray Dawson. Sookie is captured and tortured by Neave and Lochlan before Niall, Bill and Eric reach her. Bill is poisoned killing Neave and is saved by another of his maker's children. Niall kills Breandan, then closes Faery entirely and says goodbye. Crystal's killer proves to be Jason's friend Mel Hart, who is executed by the Hotshot panthers.

recaps.text: Sookie Stackhouse is a telepathic waitress in Bon Temps, Louisiana, where vampires live openly and everyone else supernatural does not. She has loved and lost Bill Compton, worked as a telepath for the vampire queen of Louisiana, and become entangled with Eric Northman, the sheriff of her territory, to whom she is bound by a blood bond. A bombing at a vampire summit in Rhodes gutted Louisiana's vampires, and Felipe de Castro, king of Nevada, then invaded the weakened state, killed the queen and took Louisiana, installing the relentlessly cheerful Victor Madden as regent over Eric. Sookie was spared as a useful asset. She has learned that she is part fairy through her great-grandfather Prince Niall Brigant, who has begun visiting her; that Bill first came to Bon Temps under orders to seduce her; and that her dead cousin Hadley left a small son, Hunter, who is telepathic like her. Her brother Jason, a werepanther, is unhappily married to Crystal Norris of the isolated Hotshot community, and the witch Amelia Broadway is still lodging upstairs.

The world's two-natured people announce themselves in a coordinated worldwide broadcast, and Sam Merlotte changes into a collie in front of his own customers to prove it. Bon Temps reacts in every direction at once: some regulars take it calmly, some stop coming, and a few become openly hostile. Sookie, who has known for years, spends her shifts managing other people's shock. Days later, Jason's wife Crystal, pregnant and long estranged from him, is found crucified on a signboard in the bar's parking lot. The murder is a public statement, timed to look like an attack on the newly revealed shapeshifters. The sheriff's office and the Hotshot werepanthers both investigate, and Jason, whose marriage was notoriously bad, is the obvious suspect to everyone but his sister.

The investigation into Crystal's death produces no answer. The panthers of Hotshot conduct their own inquiry with methods the parish sheriff would not approve of, and Jason remains under suspicion in both. Federal agents arrive in Bon Temps wanting to know how Sookie came to survive the Rhodes hotel bombing and what exactly she can do, an attention she cannot afford. Eric grows uneasy: Victor Madden's interest in Sookie is proprietary, and under the new regime a valuable human without a vampire's claim on her is simply available. Niall visits and is evasive in a new way, warning Sookie to be careful without explaining what of. A man who could pass for Jason's twin appears at the edges of events; he is Dermot, Niall's son and Sookie's great-uncle, and nobody can say whose side he is on.

The fairy quarrel comes into the open. Niall's rival Breandan wants the fae to cut every tie to the human world and holds that Niall's human-blooded descendants should be destroyed along with the connection; Sookie is the most obvious target. Eric acts before Victor Madden can: he presents Sookie with a ceremonial knife in front of witnesses, marrying her by vampire custom, which places her formally under his protection and out of the reach of anyone in Felipe de Castro's court. Guards are posted at her house, including the Shreveport werewolf Tray Dawson, and Sookie's life narrows to work, watchfulness and a house full of people carrying weapons. Meanwhile Crystal's murder still has no solution, and the town's temper about the shapeshifters continues to sour.

Breandan's people attack in earnest, and the protections around Sookie fail one at a time. Tray Dawson is killed defending her, and Claudine, her pregnant fairy godmother, is killed as well. Sookie herself is taken. Her captors are Neave and Lochlan, two fairies in Breandan's service who work on her over a period of days with deliberate, unhurried cruelty and no interest in information. She survives by refusing to give them the reaction they want and by holding on to the certainty that Niall and the vampires are looking for her, while the damage they do goes past anything she has suffered before.

Niall, Bill and Eric find Sookie and kill her captors: Bill tears out Neave's throat and Eric finishes Lochlan. Because fairy blood is poison to vampires, Bill is left dying, and Sookie has Eric track down Judith Vardamme, another child of Bill's maker, whose blood restores him. Niall kills Breandan, ending the war, and then tells Sookie that the only permanent protection for her is a closed door: he shuts Faery, stranding Claude, Dermot and the other part-fairies on the human side and taking his leave of Sookie for good. She is left maimed, badly damaged in mind as well as body, and married to Eric by vampire law. In Bon Temps the murder is finally solved: Mel Hart, Jason's quiet drinking companion, was responsible for Crystal's death and helped stage the crucifixion to look like an anti-shifter killing. The Hotshot panthers take him and settle it under their own law.

characters.description: A telepathic waitress at Merlotte's bar in Bon Temps, Louisiana, living alone in her grandmother's house and no longer able to pretend she is outside the supernatural world. She is carrying a killing nobody else knows about, a brother who has been forced into a shape he did not choose, and a growing reputation among vampires and shapeshifters as a human worth using. She is stubborn about doing right by the people she considers hers.
characters.name: Sookie Stackhouse

characters.description: Sookie's brother, a Bon Temps road crew supervisor who was kidnapped and bitten repeatedly by a werepanther the previous winter. Because he was made rather than born, his change is partial and painful: he becomes a hybrid of man and cat rather than a true panther. He faces his first full moon with his sister as his only company, and he is looking for someone to blame.
characters.name: Jason Stackhouse

characters.description: A young woman from the closed werepanther community of Hotshot who is seeing Jason Stackhouse. Her family is not pleased about the connection, and she is caught between them and him.
characters.name: Crystal Norris

characters.description: Sookie's boss, the owner of Merlotte's and a shapeshifter. He is shot in the leg outside his own bar early in the book, which puts him on crutches and leaves Sookie effectively running the place.
characters.name: Sam Merlotte

characters.description: A short-order cook newly hired at Merlotte's. She has worked kitchens in small towns all over the region, never staying long anywhere, and she is friendly enough without being anybody's friend.
characters.name: Sweetie Des Arts

characters.description: Sookie's friend from school, who runs a dress shop in Bon Temps. Her arrangement with a wealthy Mississippi vampire has been handed on to someone else without her consent, and she is frightened, bruised and unwilling to explain.
characters.name: Tara Thornton

characters.description: Sookie's former lover, the vampire who lives across the cemetery from her, returned from his travels in South America. He wants her back and she does not want him, and their dealings are civil, frequent and uncomfortable.
characters.name: Bill Compton

characters.description: The head of the Hotshot werepanther community and a road crew foreman, a steady, courteous man who has made no secret of wanting to marry Sookie. He is among those shot by the sniper working the area.
characters.name: Calvin Norris

characters.description: The thousand-year-old vampire sheriff of the area, restored to himself after the witches' curse and, as far as anyone can tell, with no memory of the weeks he spent hidden in Sookie's house. He lends Merlotte's a bartender while Sam is laid up, and he keeps finding reasons to have Sookie where he can see her.
characters.name: Eric Northman

characters.description: A small, red-haired English vampire lent to Merlotte's by Eric to tend bar while Sam recovers. Elaborately courteous, he wears an eyepatch, tells stories of a piratical life at sea, and is popular with the customers.
characters.name: Charles Twining

characters.description: The leader of the Shreveport werewolf pack, a retired air force officer who has run pack business with military discipline. His death leaves the packmaster's place open at the worst possible time.
characters.name: Colonel Flood

characters.description: The Shreveport werewolf who has twice been Sookie's ally, now backing his father's claim to lead the pack. He asks Sookie to serve as an impartial witness at the contest, which puts her in the middle of pack politics she has no standing in.
characters.name: Alcide Herveaux

characters.description: Alcide's father, who runs the family surveying company and considers himself the natural successor as packmaster. Proud, aging and heavily in debt from gambling, he is not as strong a candidate as his son believes.
characters.name: Jackson Herveaux

characters.description: A Shreveport motorcycle dealer and werewolf, the other candidate for packmaster. Ordinary-looking and widely liked among the pack's rank and file, he wants the position badly.
characters.name: Patrick Furnan

characters.description: A vampire who has taken over Tara Thornton's arrangement from her previous protector. He is small, cruel and territorial, he answers to a powerful vampire elsewhere, and he treats Tara as property to be damaged as he likes.
characters.name: Mickey

characters.description: A private investigator hired, with his wife Lily, by the Pelt family of Jackson to find out what became of their daughter Debbie. He is thorough, polite and hard to lie to, and he does not believe Sookie's account of the last time she saw her.
characters.name: Jack Leeds

characters.description: The tall, beautiful woman who appeared at Sookie's side during the fight with the witches and would not say what she was. She continues to turn up when Sookie is in danger, cheerfully unhelpful about her own nature, and admits only that looking after Sookie is a duty of hers.
characters.name: Claudine

recaps.ending: Both threats turn out to have been sitting inside Merlotte's all along. The sniper is Sweetie Des Arts, the short-order cook, who was bitten by a shapeshifter years ago, became something she despises, and has been moving from town to town killing two-natured people ever since. She corners Sookie with a rifle and is killed before she can fire, and the shootings stop. Sam, Calvin Norris and the others she wounded recover. The second threat is Charles Twining, the courteous English vampire Eric lent to the bar. He set the fire at Sookie's house and he attacks her openly at the end: he was sent to Louisiana to avenge Long Shadow, the vampire Eric destroyed at Fangtasia years earlier, and killing Eric's favorite human was the closest he could get. He is destroyed. The werewolf pack ends the book under Patrick Furnan, who cheated his way through the contest; Jackson Herveaux is dead, and Alcide, who blames Sookie for not preventing it, is no longer easy company. Tara Thornton is free of Mickey, bought out of the arrangement by Eric at a price Sookie will owe. Bill is back in Bon Temps and unwelcome. The last word belongs to Eric, who tells Sookie that his memory has come back: he remembers the weeks in her house, their nights together, and Debbie Pelt dying on her kitchen floor, which means Sookie's one real secret is now shared with the most dangerous person she knows.
recaps.in_short: Sookie sees her brother Jason through his first full moon as a bitten werepanther, then finds that someone is shooting shapeshifters across the parish: Sam Merlotte is hit in the leg, Calvin Norris is wounded, and a young woman is killed. Running the bar in Sam's place, Sookie takes on a vampire bartender lent by Eric, an Englishman named Charles Twining. Her house is set on fire in the night and she barely escapes. Meanwhile the Shreveport werewolf pack loses its leader and holds a contest to replace him; Sookie is asked to witness, sees Patrick Furnan cheat, and cannot stop the contest that kills Alcide's father. Private investigators hired by Debbie Pelt's family press her about the disappearance she is responsible for, and she has to get Eric's help to free her friend Tara from a brutal vampire. Sookie works out that the sniper is Sweetie Des Arts, the bar's own cook, a woman bitten years ago who hates what she became; Sweetie is killed. Charles then attacks Sookie, revealed as an assassin avenging a vampire Eric destroyed, and is destroyed himself. Eric ends the book by telling Sookie that he remembers everything.

recaps.text: Sookie Stackhouse is a telepathic waitress at Merlotte's bar in Bon Temps, Louisiana, in a world where vampires live openly. Her grandmother was murdered by a man hunting Sookie; her boss Sam Merlotte is a shapeshifter; and she has survived a maenad, the anti-vampire Fellowship of the Sun, and a vampire kingdom's politics. Her relationship with the vampire Bill Compton ended after he planned to leave her for his maker and then, starving and out of his mind, nearly killed her during his own rescue in Mississippi; she killed his maker herself. She is watched, wanted and repeatedly used by Eric Northman, the thousand-year-old sheriff of the area. Last winter a coven cursed Eric with amnesia, Sookie hid him in her house for pay, and they became lovers; when the curse broke he remembered none of it. On the same night, Debbie Pelt broke in to kill Sookie and Sookie shot her dead, a killing Eric helped conceal and then forgot, leaving Sookie the only person who knows. Her brother Jason was kidnapped and bitten by a werepanther from the isolated community of Hotshot and will now change with the full moon. Sookie is also guarded, on and off, by a beautiful woman named Claudine who will not explain what she is.

Sookie spends the first full moon of Jason's new life with him, out at his house by the pond, because there is no one else to do it. Because he was bitten rather than born to it, his change is partial and agonizing and leaves him a hybrid of man and cat, an object of contempt to the born werepanthers of Hotshot. He is furious about it and looking for someone to punish. Back in town, Sam Merlotte is shot in the leg by a rifle as he steps out of Merlotte's, and the bar is left without an owner on his feet. Sookie takes on the running of it, hires help, and starts hearing about other shootings in the area. The victims have nothing obvious in common until Sookie sees what the police cannot: every one of them is two-natured.

The shootings continue. Calvin Norris, the head of Hotshot, is badly wounded, and a young woman is killed outright, and the shapeshifter community of the parish realizes it is being hunted by someone who knows what they are. Sookie, who now has to keep Merlotte's staffed at night, accepts Eric Northman's offer of a bartender: Charles Twining, a small, courteous English vampire with an eyepatch and a stock of stories about a life at sea, who proves to be very good with customers. Bill Compton comes home from South America and starts finding reasons to be near Sookie, who does not want him back. The Shreveport werewolf pack loses Colonel Flood, its longtime leader, and the pack's succession is suddenly an open question.

Alcide Herveaux asks Sookie to serve as an impartial witness at the contest that will decide the next packmaster, between his father Jackson Herveaux and Patrick Furnan, a motorcycle dealer with the rank and file behind him. Sookie also has her friend Tara Thornton to worry about: Tara's arrangement with a wealthy vampire has been handed on to Mickey, a vicious vampire who is hurting her and whom Tara is too frightened to leave. Sookie asks Eric for help, which costs her. On top of that, private investigators hired by Debbie Pelt's family arrive from Jackson, asking careful questions about the night Debbie disappeared, and Sookie, who shot her, has to lie to their faces without any assurance that they believe her.

Sookie's house is set on fire in the night. She gets out alive, but part of the house is gutted, most of what her grandmother left her is ruined, and a man's body is found in the burned area. She is left camping in what remains and depending on the goodwill of people she does not entirely trust, with money from the pack and the vampires paying for the repairs. Eric handles Mickey, and Tara is freed from him at a price that will be Sookie's to pay eventually. Between the sniper, the arson, the pack's succession fight and the Pelts' investigators, Sookie cannot tell which of the several people circling her is the one actually trying to kill her.

The packmaster contest is held, and Sookie, witnessing, sees Patrick Furnan cheat in one of the trials. She cannot stop what follows: the contest ends in a fight to the death, and Jackson Herveaux is killed. Furnan becomes packmaster of Shreveport. Alcide, grieving and looking for a reason, blames Sookie for not preventing it, and the friendship between them goes cold. Sookie, meanwhile, works out the pattern behind the shootings by thinking about who has been present in every town where a shapeshifter was shot, rather than about who hates them.

The sniper is Sweetie Des Arts, the short-order cook at Merlotte's, who was bitten by a shapeshifter years ago, became a thing she cannot stand being, and has since moved from town to town killing two-natured people. She corners Sookie with the rifle and is killed before she can use it, and the shootings end. That same night Charles Twining attacks Sookie in the open. The polite English bartender was sent to Louisiana to avenge Long Shadow, the vampire Eric destroyed at Fangtasia years ago; he set the fire at Sookie's house, and killing Eric's favorite human was the nearest thing to revenge available to him. He is destroyed. Sam recovers, Tara is free of Mickey, and Sookie is left with a half-burned house and a ruined friendship with Alcide. Then Eric comes to tell her that his memory has returned: he remembers the weeks in her house, what they were to each other, and Debbie Pelt dying on her kitchen floor.

characters.description: Chicago's professional wizard, now sharing his tiny basement apartment with his half-brother Thomas and a rapidly growing dog. With Murphy out of town, Harry is blackmailed into a hunt for a dead necromancer's lost book while the necromancer's surviving disciples descend on Chicago for Halloween, each meaning to use what the book unlocks to seize godlike power. Maimed hand, mounting debts to dark powers, and a war still on his shoulders - and still nobody better positioned to stand in the way.
characters.name: Harry Dresden

characters.description: Harry's half-brother, the White Court vampire, now sleeping on Harry's couch after being cut off by his family. Thomas is struggling - trying to hold down mortal jobs, trying not to feed, and chafing against everything his nature demands - and the friction of two proud, private men sharing one small apartment runs through the book. When the fighting starts, he is exactly the ally a wizard wants at his back.
characters.name: Thomas Raith

characters.description: The ancient Black Court vampire, neither dead nor done with Harry. Mavra opens the book with blackmail: she holds evidence that could destroy Karrin Murphy's career and freedom, and she will use it unless Harry finds her a legendary necromancer's lost text, The Word of Kemmler, within three days. Cold, patient, and untroubled by the apocalyptic potential of what she is asking for, she sets the whole plot in motion.
characters.name: Mavra

characters.description: A slight, wiry, polka-loving medical examiner - the one who was institutionalized for reporting the truth about corpses that were not human. Waldo Butters is no fighter and makes no pretense of courage, which is exactly what makes his courage matter: dragged into the necromancers' war over the bodies in his morgue, he stays, helps, and grows. His medical skill, his curiosity, and his one-man polka band all turn out to be surprisingly load-bearing.
characters.name: Waldo Butters

characters.description: The spirit of intellect in the skull in Harry's lab - and, this case reveals, a store of darker history than Harry knew. Bob's knowledge of necromancy is firsthand: the skull once served Heinrich Kemmler himself, the necromancer whose disciples are converging on Chicago, and there is a part of Bob's own past that Harry must handle with extreme care. His lore on the Erlking and on Kemmler's methods becomes the key to everything.
characters.name: Bob

characters.description: Harry's dog, no longer a puppy: a huge, gray, preternaturally intelligent Foo dog whose senses for the uncanny outstrip any ward. Mouse is calm, deliberate, and devoted, and in this book he proves he is not merely large but genuinely supernatural - an ally in his own right when the dead start walking.
characters.name: Mouse

characters.description: The most straightforwardly brutal of Kemmler's surviving disciples: a tall, cadaverous necromancer who walks Chicago with an entourage of zombies and a habit of raising the freshly dead as enforcers. Grevane wants the Word of Kemmler and the power it unlocks, and he interrogates, kills, and animates his way toward it. Of the rivals converging on the city, he is the bluntest instrument - which does not make him the least dangerous.
characters.name: Grevane

characters.description: A necromancer in a concealing hood and cloak whose power dwarfs the other disciples - in a direct clash, more than a match for Harry. Cowl speaks with dry courtesy, works with a similarly hooded partner called Kumori, and his true identity stays hidden behind the cowl he is named for. Of everyone hunting Kemmler's legacy, he is the one whose plans reach furthest, and the one Harry has the least idea how to stop.
characters.name: Cowl

characters.description: A disciple of Kemmler whose specialty is the theft of bodies: the Corpsetaker trades minds with victims, wearing stolen flesh and discarding it, so that no face can be trusted twice. Ancient, cunning, and patient, the Corpsetaker hunts the Word of Kemmler alongside the other disciples, and the body-swapping makes every encounter a potential ambush from inside someone Harry trusts.
characters.name: The Corpsetaker

characters.description: The shadow of the fallen angel whose coin Harry buried under his lab - present in his mind since the day he touched it, and in this book, no longer silent. The shadow can shape what Harry perceives, offers him knowledge and power with perfect helpfulness, and wants exactly what every Denarian's coin wants: for Harry to take up the real thing. Its unmasking forces Harry to reckon with what he has been carrying for the past year.
characters.name: Lasciel's shadow

characters.description: Captain of the Wardens of the White Council, the wizards' soldiers and enforcers. Luccio arrives in Chicago with a battered handful of Wardens - the corps has been gutted by the vampire war - to face the necromancer crisis. A career soldier of centuries' standing, forthright and fair, she weighs Harry by what he does rather than by his file, and what happens to her in Chicago changes her life permanently.
characters.name: Anastasia Luccio

recaps.ending: The Darkhallow fails. On Halloween night, with the city's dead walking, Harry disrupts the ritual that would have made one of Kemmler's disciples a god: the vast well of spiritual power is never claimed, and the storm of necromancy breaks. Grevane and the Corpsetaker fall out and fight among themselves; Grevane dies in the chaos, and Harry personally shoots the Corpsetaker after realizing the mind-swapping necromancer had stolen the body of Warden-Captain Luccio - leaving Luccio alive but permanently housed in the young body the Corpsetaker had been wearing. Cowl is buried in the collapse of his own ritual, no corpse ever confirmed. Harry's improbable cavalry is the book's signature image: using Kemmler's own methods, he animates Sue, the museum's Tyrannosaurus skeleton, and rides her into the battle with Butters drumming the polka beat that sustains the spell. The fallen Denarian Cassius dies in an earlier ambush, spitting a death curse at Harry: die alone. In the aftermath, the decimated White Council drafts Harry into the Wardens as regional commander for the central United States - the wizard cops who once watched him for a chance to execute him now issue him a gray cloak - and Luccio's own sword-forging talent is lost with her old body. Mavra's blackmail hold over Murphy is broken, Butters has found his courage, and Harry has admitted at last that the shadow of Lasciel lives in his head - an enemy inside the walls, still there as the book closes.
recaps.in_short: With Murphy away, the vampire Mavra blackmails Harry - evidence that would destroy Murphy's career against the recovery of The Word of Kemmler, the lost book of history's worst necromancer. Kemmler's surviving disciples - zombie-raising Grevane, the body-stealing Corpsetaker, and the hooded, hugely powerful Cowl - converge on Chicago to use the book for the Darkhallow, a Halloween ritual to devour the city's dead and ascend to godhood. Aided by his brother Thomas, the skull-spirit Bob (who once served Kemmler himself), his Foo dog Mouse, and the timid, polka-loving medical examiner Waldo Butters, Harry fights zombie hordes, survives the Denarian Cassius's ambush and death curse, summons the Erlking's wild hunt into his enemies' path, and finally admits the shadow of the fallen angel Lasciel has been living in his mind since Death Masks. On Halloween night he animates Sue, the museum's T. rex skeleton, rides her into battle, and breaks the Darkhallow: Grevane dies, Harry kills the Corpsetaker - who had body-swapped with Warden-Captain Luccio, leaving her in a young stranger's body - and Cowl vanishes in the collapse. The gutted White Council drafts Harry into the Wardens, and Murphy is safe.

recaps.text: Previously: Harry Dresden learned that Thomas Raith, the White Court vampire who kept saving his life, is his half-brother - both sons of Margaret LeFay, whom the White King, Lord Raith, murdered. Harry and Thomas survived Raith's trap; their mother's death curse had secretly left the king powerless, and Lara Raith now rules the White Court behind her father's figurehead throne. Thomas, cut off from his family, moved into Harry's apartment. The costs are mounting: Harry's left hand was burned nearly useless in a daylight raid on the Black Court vampire Mavra's nest - a raid made with Murphy and the mercenary Kincaid - and he learned his old mentor Ebenezar McCoy is the Blackstaff, the Council's secret assassin. Harry still hides the shadow of the fallen angel Lasciel, taken into his mind when he grabbed her coin to save a child; the coin lies buried under his lab. The wizards' war with the Red Court grinds on, and the Wardens are being bled dry.

With Murphy on holiday with Kincaid, Mavra of the Black Court comes to collect her grudge in a new currency: blackmail. She holds evidence that would send Murphy to prison, and her price is The Word of Kemmler - the lost final text of Heinrich Kemmler, the necromancer so terrible the White Council killed him seven times - delivered within three days. Harry starts hunting the book and immediately trips over the competition: Grevane, a disciple of Kemmler, is in Chicago with an entourage of zombies, tearing through anyone connected to the text. At the morgue, medical examiner Waldo Butters shows Harry bodies that mark the killers' trail, and promptly gets dragged along when the trail doubles back onto them. Bob the skull, it emerges, knows Kemmler's work uncomfortably well.

The field grows crowded: besides Grevane there is the Corpsetaker, an ancient horror who swaps minds with victims and wears their stolen bodies, and Cowl, a hooded necromancer whose raw power exceeds anything Harry can match head-on - each disciple hunting the Word, each planning to use it on Halloween night for the Darkhallow, a ritual that would devour the spirits of the city's dead and elevate its caster to godhood. Harry learns Bob's buried history - the skull once served Kemmler himself - and recovers a darker sub-personality of the spirit with great care. Attacks and reprisals escalate: zombies against wards, ghouls in the streets, and Harry, Thomas, Butters and Mouse increasingly under siege. The numbers say Harry cannot beat even one disciple in open battle, let alone three.

Harry works the angles instead of the head-on fight. Deciphering Kemmler's methods with Bob, he identifies what the Darkhallow needs - and what might wreck it.
